title: Local duals of integral constructible sheaves
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $\pi_E$ a uniformizer, and $X$ a scheme. The coefficient sheaf on a scheme $T$ is the completed sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}\cong\varprojlim_n(A/\pi_E^n)_T$, not the constant sheaf $\underline A$ [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Let $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and let $S$ be a stratum on which $C$ is pro-étale locally the completion of a finitely generated $A$-module: there are a pro-étale cover $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ and finitely generated $A$-modules $N_i$, which may depend on $i$, with $C|_{U_i}\simeq\mathcal O_{E,U_i}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{N_i}$ for every $i$ (the local-model convention of [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model]). Then $C|_S$ is dualizable in $D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, with dual $C^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}(C|_S,\mathcal O_{E,S})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]: there are evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying both triangle identities. The complex $C|_S$ has Tor amplitude in $[-1,0]$, and $C^\vee$ has Tor amplitude in $[0,1]$, where Tor amplitude tests derived tensor against every sheaf of $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For $C=\mathcal O_{E,X}/\pi_E$, one has $C^\vee\simeq(\mathcal O_{E,S}/\pi_E)[-1]$.

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O_{E,S}$ and $K=C|_S$, in degree zero. Fix a chart $U=U_i$ of the assumed cover and write $N=N_i$, so $K_U=R_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline N$; the following construction is made separately on each chart, so the modules, and the integers $a,b$ below, may vary with $i$. The coefficient-ring lemma says that $A$ is a DVR and a PID; hence every ideal is finitely generated, so $A$ is Noetherian. Choose finitely many generators of $N$, giving a surjection $A^b\to N$. Its kernel $L$ is finitely generated by the Noetherian-submodule lemma. It is torsion-free: if $0\ne t\in A$ and $t v=0$ in $L\subset A^b$, each coordinate of $v$ is zero because $A$ is a domain. The finite torsion-free DVR-module lemma gives $L\simeq A^a$ for finite $a$. Thus $0\to A^a\xrightarrow{\phi}A^b\to N\to0$ is exact. This constructs the length-one resolution, rather than positing it as another node.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences; algebra inputs: Stacks 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic) and 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3)

proof.text: On a chart $U$, the integral-limit identification gives $R_U=\varprojlim_n\underline{A/\pi_E^n}$. Apply the completed-constant-sheaf lemma with $T=U$ and $I=(\pi_E)$: $R_U$ is flat over $\underline A$. Part (1) of the constant-module-section lemma sends the preceding module sequence to a short exact sequence of constant sheaves (indeed, it is exact on every object). Tensoring it with $R_U$ is exact by the stated flatness. Consequently $P_U=[R_U^a\xrightarrow{\phi}R_U^b]$, in degrees $-1,0$, has its augmentation to $K_U$ as a quasi-isomorphism. The tensor here is over the constant sheaf $\underline A$; the tensor products used below are over the completed ring sheaf $R$ or $R_U$.

source.place: Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact) and 093M (lemma-completion-flat); coefficient limit is supplied by the cited integral-limit statement

proof.text: Use the small site skeletons and universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Slice restriction is exact by the restriction lemma, so it commutes with kernels, cokernels and cohomology and sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. For the localization morphism, the inverse image is slice restriction, with right adjoint $H\mapsto(V\mapsto H(V\times_S U\to U))$; the adjunction maps are induced by the projections and diagonal, and restriction preserves finite limits sectionwise. Apply the derived-tensor-pullback lemma to this morphism with ring $R_U=R|_U$; its module pullback is this exact restriction. It follows that restriction commutes with derived tensor. The internal-Hom restriction lemma also gives $R\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)|_U\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(L|_U,M|_U)$ without boundedness assumptions. Finally a morphism in $D(R)$ is an isomorphism if it is one on every chart: apply the sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism lemma to each cohomology-sheaf map and then the unbounded-derived cohomology criterion, which states exactly that all these isomorphisms imply the derived map is an isomorphism. Its covers-top hypothesis holds because base change of the given cover covers every site object. The same argument applied to $0\to H^q(L)$ detects vanishing of cohomology locally. This uses locality only for isomorphisms and vanishing, not for equality of derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); derived pullback/tensor compatibility as in Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); cohomology-sheaf local test written out

proof.text:
Normalize the closed structure so that its adjunction is the standard sheaf derived-Hom adjunction. For standard $H(L,M)=R\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)$, the internal-Hom currying isomorphism and the global-sections identification give natural bijections
$\operatorname{Hom}(B,H(L,M))\simeq H^0(S,H(B,H(L,M)))\simeq H^0(S,H(B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L,M))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L,M)$.
Thus $H(L,-)$ represents the right adjoint to $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$; by symmetry it is the internal Hom of the coefficient category specified in the derived-tensor-Hom definition. Concretely the two comparisons between these right-adjoint objects are obtained by transposing their counits, and their composites transpose back to the same counits, so are identities. We may therefore use this specific natural adjunction and its evaluation. Put $D=H(K,R)$ and let $e:D\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to R$ be the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_D$. The currying and restriction constructions are canonical, so their restricted adjunctions and evaluations agree with those on each chart.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); degree-zero Hom identification supplied by lem-pur-rhom-global-sections; formal representing-object comparison written out

proof.text:
By restriction compatibility and the bounded-free derived-Hom model, $D|_U$ is represented by $Q_U=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_U,R_U[0])$. The model applies with $P_U^i=0$ for $i>0$, target zero in degrees $<0$, and globally finite free source terms on this slice. Its differential formula gives
$Q_U=[(R_U^b)^\vee\xrightarrow{-\phi^T}(R_U^a)^\vee]$ in degrees $0,1$, with the displayed terms identified with $R_U^b,R_U^a$. The minus sign is the cochain-Hom convention; negating the degree-one term identifies this with the positive-transpose convention. Finite free sheaves are flat because tensoring with $R_U^r$ is a finite direct sum of the identity functor, which preserves short exact sequences. Thus both $P_U$ and $Q_U$ are bounded-above complexes of flat sheaves, and the bounded-above-flat lemma makes both K-flat.

Let $G$ be any sheaf of $R$-modules, placed in degree zero. On a chart, compute $K_U\otimes_{R_U}^{\mathbf L}G_U$ by $P_U\otimes_{R_U}G_U$ and $D_U\otimes_{R_U}^{\mathbf L}G_U$ by $Q_U\otimes_{R_U}G_U$, using the K-flat computation in the derived-tensor definition. These complexes have zero terms outside $[-1,0]$ and $[0,1]$, respectively, hence zero cohomology there. Restriction commutes with tensor and cohomology by step 3; the local vanishing test gives the same bounds globally. This proves exactly the two Tor-amplitude assertions in the constructibility definition, since $G$ was arbitrary, with no flatness, finite generation or constructibility imposed on $G$.

source.place: Proof, Tor-amplitude sentences; the term-support argument is written out

proof.text:
Define a global map $\alpha:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D\to H(K,K)$ as the transpose, under step 4, of
$(K\otimes D)\otimes K\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes e}K$,
with the canonical associators and unitors understood. On a chart use the K-flat model $Q_U$ for $D_U$. Since $K_U$ is itself a degree-zero sheaf, the source is represented by $K_U\otimes Q_U$. The bounded-free derived-Hom lemma applied with source $P_U$ and target $K_U[0]$ represents the target by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_U,K_U)$. In both complexes the degree-zero and degree-one terms are $K_U^b$ and $K_U^a$, and the differential is $-\phi^T$. For a finite free term $R_U^r$ with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ and dual basis $e_1^*,\ldots,e_r^*$, the evaluation map $K_U\otimes(R_U^r)^\vee\to\mathcal Hom(R_U^r,K_U)$ sends $x\otimes f$ to $(p\mapsto f(p)x)$. Its inverse sends a local map $h$ to $\sum_{j=1}^r h(e_j)\otimes e_j^*$; the two composites are identities by expansion in the basis, and these formulas commute with restriction, so they are inverse sheaf morphisms. This also covers $r=0$. In degrees zero and one the evaluation maps commute with the differential $-\phi^T$, since precomposition with $\phi$ sends the coordinate vector $(x_j)$ to $(\sum_j\phi_{ji}x_j)_i$ on both sides. It represents the restricted $\alpha$ by the defining evaluation adjunction. Thus $\alpha|_U$ is an isomorphism. The cohomology-sheaf test of step 3 proves that the single global map $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), canonical comparison specialized to M=K; Tag 08JI supplies the bounded-target Hom computation

proof.text:
Let $u:R\to H(K,K)$ be the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_K$ under step 4 and define the global coevaluation $\eta=\alpha^{-1}u:R\to K\otimes D$. Naturality of the adjunction in its left argument says that the transpose of $\alpha\eta$ is
$f=(1_K\otimes e)(\eta\otimes1_K):K\to K$.
But $\alpha\eta=u$, whose transpose is $\mathrm{id}_K$. Hence $f=\mathrm{id}_K$, the first triangle identity. This constructs a global map by an inverse isomorphism, without gluing locally chosen morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0FPU (example-dual-derived); first omitted triangle verification supplied explicitly

proof.text:
For the other triangle put $g=(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes\eta):D\to D$. Bifunctoriality of tensor gives
$e(g\otimes1_K)=e(1_D\otimes f)$:
after expanding $g$ and $f$, both sides insert $1_D\otimes\eta\otimes1_K$ to reach $D\otimes K\otimes D\otimes K$ and then apply $e\otimes e$, followed by the unit identification $R\otimes R\simeq R$; the two orders of applying the evaluations coincide by interchange. The first triangle makes this composite $e$. The adjunction bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}(D,H(K,R))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(D\otimes K,R)$
sends $g$ to $e(g\otimes1_K)$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$ to $e$. Its injectivity yields $g=\mathrm{id}_D$. Both triangle identities therefore hold globally, which is precisely dualizability of $K$ with dual $D$.

source.place: Tag 0FPU (example-dual-derived); second omitted triangle verification supplied explicitly

proof.text:
For $C=\mathcal O_{E,X}/\pi_E$, use the coefficient resolution statement with scheme $S$ and $n=1$:
$0\to R\xrightarrow{\pi_E}R\to (A/\pi_E)_S\to0$.
Thus $K=R/\pi_E=(A/\pi_E)_S$ has the global two-term resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\pi_E}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The bounded-free Hom computation gives its dual $[R\xrightarrow{-\pi_E}R]$ in degrees $0,1$. The differential is injective by the same exact sequence and its cokernel is $R/\pi_E$, so the quotient chain map to $(R/\pi_E)[-1]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In the cohomological shift convention the latter sheaf occupies degree $1$. This proves the example, including its sign and shift.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences; coefficient resolution plus the cochain-Hom differential supplies the shift

proof_origin.place: Proof; follows the two-term free-resolution route, with the global canonical-map argument of Stacks 08JJ/0FPU and both triangle calculations supplied explicitly

split_report.summary: Expanded the local length-one scalar resolution, exact constant/completed transport, ringed-site dual model, arbitrary-module Tor bounds and torsion example. Replaced the invalid local-equality inference in the blueprint by a globally defined canonical comparison, its locally checked isomorphism, and global adjunction proofs of both triangles. Made the implicit finite-extension/coefficient conventions explicit; no finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis on X or S is needed because the local model is assumed. Reused existing nodes only; checked each cited statement and searched for exact Lean and Mathlib attachments. Landing-return repair: refreshed every direct dependency against the current DAG and replaced the finite-projective evaluation citation by the explicit finite-free basis/inverse calculation in step 7, avoiding the stale perfect-evaluation path and unnecessary general site hypotheses.
split_report.blueprint: Proof first three sentences: steps 1–2. Termwise dual: step 5. Locality, canonical evaluation and coevaluation: steps 3–4 and 7–9, correcting the source gluing/local-equality shortcut. Tor-amplitude sentences: step 6. Residue example: step 10. These realize unit steps 4–5 without changing their two-term-resolution route.

tool_uses.why: The unit needs the scalar ring to be a DVR/PID; this coefficient-algebra tool supplies that property, not another proof route.
Finite generation of the presentation kernel is elementary Noetherian-module infrastructure, absent from this unit.
The unit calls for a length-one finite free resolution; this DVR algebra fact makes its finite torsion-free kernel free.
Identifies the completed coefficient sheaf with the limit required by the flatness tool; the unit does not construct the coefficient ring.
Only the flatness of constant-to-completed coefficients is used, exactly at the completion step prescribed by the unit.
Part (1) transports the scalar short exact presentation to constant sheaves; general site infrastructure absent from the unit.
Fixes small site skeletons in a universe containing schemes and module categories, as required by the generic site tools.
Exactness of slice restriction justifies cohomology and quasi-isomorphism restriction; the unit does not prove this generic site fact.
Localizes derived tensor to a pro-etale chart; a ringed-site tool needed to read off the unit Tor bounds.
Uses precisely its currying and slice-restriction clauses to globalize the two-term dual construction, without replacing the unit route.
Detects isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves on the chosen cover; no assertion of local detection of derived morphism equality is used.
The existing general Mathlib leaf converts isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves to a derived isomorphism; no hypothesis of boundedness is imposed.
The degree-zero identification converts standard sheaf-derived-Hom currying to an adjunction on derived morphisms; absent from the unit.
Fixes the relative completed-coefficient tensor, K-flat computation and closed adjunction used throughout.
Computes sheaf RHom from the bounded finite free resolution, both with targets R and K; generic ringed-site algebra, not a six-functor substitute.
Makes the displayed bounded finite free complexes K-flat so their ordinary tensors compute the required derived tensors.
Supplies the given local-model and arbitrary-module Tor-amplitude conventions.
Only its short exact coefficient resolution at n=1 is used to compute the explicit residue example.

The blueprint's 'hold locally, hence globally' is a real error (the H^1(S^1,Z) example is correct), and the global-map repair keeps the two-term-resolution route.
